output.summary: KEP-1792 adds an opt-in PodSpec field that sets a pod's kernel hostname (nodename) to its FQDN instead of its shortname. The KEP is at implementable status, stage beta, owned by sig-node.
output.rationale: Legacy applications, especially on RedHat/CentOS-style systems, expect the kernel hostname to be the FQDN, and containerizing them without code changes is hard. The field defaults to false so existing behavior is preserved. Reviewers chose a PodSpec field over a kubelet flag so that controllers such as Deployments behave consistently across their pods.

alternatives.option: Make users fix legacy code to not assume the FQDN is the hostname
alternatives.why_not: Described in the KEP as not practical.
Configuration flags are harder to maintain and require platforms such as GKE to support them; a PodSpec flag keeps behavior consistent across pods of the same controller.

alternatives.option: Admission plugin that checks FQDN length
alternatives.why_not: Might not cover all pod entry points (Deployments, ReplicaSets, CRDs, etc.) and breaks abstraction layers; reviewer thockin suggested it would only shift the error up-stack, and proposed an example admission controller instead.

alternatives.option: Non-retriable pod errors that move the pod to Failed
alternatives.why_not: Listed as an alternative for improving the failure mode; the sources do not record a decision on it.

evidence.quote: The new PodSpec field `setHostnameAsFQDN` will default to `false` to preserve current behavior, i.e., setting the hostname field of the kernel to the pod's shortname.
Having this feature would help containerize existing applications without deep, risky code changes.
Additionally, using a PodSpec flag we ensure that the behavior of controllers, like Deployments, is consistent on all its pods.
As discussed today, I don't think this will actually make it better, it will just shift the error up-stack.
We're generally trying to have 2 releases between Beta and GA - I recommend targetting GA for 1.22.
